The evidence suggests that Dehrodiisoeugenol acts as a target for Cytochrome c4, which in turn is targeted by (14R,16R)-4'-(dichloromethyl)-5',7,9,13-tetramethylspiro[5-oxapentacyclo[10.8.0.02,9.04,8.013,18]icos-18-ene-6,2'-oxane]-14,16-diol. This compound is ultimately targeted by Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, indicating a chain of interactions that may involve the transport of an anionic molecule across cellular membranes. The scores from the paths suggest a plausible, though not fully elucidated, pathway where Dehrodiisoeugenol influences the activity of Cytochrome c4, which then modulates the activity of the transporter. The integrated evidence supports a mechanistic link between Dehrodiisoeugenol and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, though the exact nature of the interactions and the role of intermediate compounds remains to be fully characterized.
